{{神社| 名称=坂手神社| 所在地=愛知県一宮市佐千原宮東91| 位置=| 祭神=[[高水上神]]| 社格=式内社・旧県社| 創建=不明| }}
'''坂手神社'''（さかてじんじゃ）は、[[愛知県]][[一宮市]]にある[[神社]]である。旧[[社格]]は県社。
[[延喜式神名帳|式内社]]の[[尾張国]][[中島郡]]「坂手神社」という（別説として、[[稲沢市]]の日吉社がある）。坂手神社のある地は尾張国[[葉栗郡]]であるが、中世以前は中島郡と推測されている。地名の佐千原（さちはら）は、坂手から佐手原、佐千原と変化した地名という。
明治時代までは、毎年[[伊勢神宮]]より幣錦を賜っていた。一説には[[伊勢神宮]]の御厨であったという。[[元伊勢]]の[[尾張国]]中嶋宮と伝えられている（中嶋宮は[[酒見神社]]の説もある）。
== 概況 == *創建時期は不明。[[垂仁天皇]]14年、[[天照大神]]の御霊代を祀る地を探していた[[倭姫命]]は、[[美濃国]]伊久良河宮（現[[天神神社 (瑞穂市)|天神神社]]）から尾張国中島郡にたどりつく。この地に坂手大神を祀ったのが最初という。天照大神の御霊代は現在の坂手神社のやや北に仮宮を築き祀ったという。 *江戸時代は八剣社と称されていたが、[[1872年]]（明治5年）に郷社、[[1941]]年（昭和16年）に県社となる。
== 祭神 == *[[高水上神]] :[[オオヤマツミ|大山祗神]]の息子神とされている。
== 所在地 == *愛知県一宮市佐千原宮東91
== 交通機関 == *[[名鉄バス]]「佐千原」バス停下車、徒歩15分。または「東佐千原」バス停下車、徒歩10分 **[[名古屋鉄道]][[名鉄名古屋本線|名古屋本線]]・[[名鉄尾西線|尾西線]][[名鉄一宮駅]]、[[東海道本線]][[尾張一宮駅]]（[[名鉄一宮駅バスターミナル]]3番のりば）より「宮田本郷」「川島」行き ::「佐千原」バス停は「宮田本郷」行き、「東佐千原」バス停は「川島」行き
{{DEFAULTSORT:さかてしんしや}} [[Category:愛知県の神社]] [[Category:一宮市]] {{shinto-stub}}

明治時代までは、毎年[[伊勢神宮]]より幣錦を賜っていた。一説には[[伊勢神宮]]の御厨であったという。[[元伊勢]]の[[尾張国]]中嶋宮と伝えられている（中嶋宮は[[酒見神社]]の説もある）。
== 概況 == *創建時期は不明。[[垂仁天皇]]14年、[[天照大神]]の御霊代を祀る地を探していた[[倭姫命]]は、[[美濃国]]伊久良河宮（現[[天神神社 (瑞穂市)|天神神社]]）から尾張国中島郡にたどりつく。この地に坂手大神を祀ったのが最初という。天照大神の御霊代は現在の坂手神社のやや北に仮宮を築き祀ったという。 *江戸時代は八剣社と称されていたが、[[1872年]]（明治5年）に郷社、[[1941年]]（昭和16年）に県社となる。
== 祭神 == *[[高水上神]] :[[オオヤマツミ|大山祗神]]の息子神とされている。
== 交通機関 == *[[名鉄バス]]「佐千原」バス停下車、徒歩15分。または「東佐千原」バス停下車、徒歩10分 **[[名古屋鉄道]][[名鉄名古屋本線|名古屋本線]]・[[名鉄尾西線|尾西線]][[名鉄一宮駅]]、[[東海道本線]][[尾張一宮駅]]（[[名鉄一宮駅バスターミナル]]3番のりば）より「宮田本郷」「川島」行き ::「佐千原」バス停は「宮田本郷」行き、「東佐千原」バス停は「川島」行き

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|qq=|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|qq=|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|qq=|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|qq=|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|qq=|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|qq=|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|qq=|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|qq=|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|qq=|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|qq=|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|qq=|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|qq=|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|qq=|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|qq=|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|qq=|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|qq=|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

More sources to add<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Authors|first=Various|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XEIiEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA534|title=RLE: Japan Mini-Set F: Philosophy and Religion (4 vols)|date=2021-03-18|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-90356-4|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nPaezHFlfNQC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT107|title=Where the Trees Grow Thick|isbn=978-0-595-28240-1|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Göttler|first1=Christine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uyk_DwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA437|title=The Nomadic Object: The Challenge of World for Early Modern Religious Art|last2=Mochizuki|first2=Mia|date=2017-11-06|publisher=BRILL|isbn=978-90-04-35450-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Picken|first=Stuart D. == Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

More sources to add<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Authors|first=Various|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XEIiEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA534|title=RLE: Japan Mini-Set F: Philosophy and Religion (4 vols)|date=2021-03-18|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-90356-4|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nPaezHFlfNQC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT107|title=Where the Trees Grow Thick|isbn=978-0-595-28240-1|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Göttler|first1=Christine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uyk_DwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA437|title=The Nomadic Object: The Challenge of World for Early Modern Religious Art|last2=Mochizuki|first2=Mia|date=2017-11-06|publisher=BRILL|isbn=978-90-04-35450-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Picken|first=Stuart D. == Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.
