'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

More sources to add<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. == Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in [[:en:Aichi Prefecture|Aichi Prefecture]]'s city of [[:en:Ichinomiya, Aichi|Ichinomiya]]. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, [[:en:Owari Province|Owari Province]] (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in [[:en:Inazawa|Inazawa]]). Although the shrine is located in [[:en:Haguri District|Haguri District]] of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of [[:en:Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suinin]], [[:en:Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Yamato-hime-no-mikoto]]—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu]]—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of [[:en:Ōyamatsumi|Ōyamatsumi]].

== Access ==

* Take the [[:en:Meitetsu Bus|Meitetsu Bus]] to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From [[:en:Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station]] (platform 3, bus terminal) on the [[:en:Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line]] & Bisai Line and [[:en:Owari-Ichinomiya Station|JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station]].
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.
