== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture}}'s city of {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|en|Ichinomiya, Aichi|WD=Q270810|lt=Ichinomiya}}. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province}} (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|lt=Inazawa}}). Although the shrine is located in {{ill|Haguri District|en|Haguri District|WD=Q1032507|lt=Haguri District}} of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}} annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

More sources to add<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Authors|first=Various|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XEIiEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA534|title=RLE: Japan Mini-Set F: Philosophy and Religion (4 vols)|date=2021-03-18|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-90356-4|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nPaezHFlfNQC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT107|title=Where the Trees Grow Thick|isbn=978-0-595-28240-1|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Göttler|first1=Christine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uyk_DwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA437|title=The Nomadic Object: The Challenge of World for Early Modern Religious Art|last2=Mochizuki|first2=Mia|date=2017-11-06|publisher=BRILL|isbn=978-90-04-35450-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Picken|first=Stuart D. B.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xlG3F6gSm9UC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA232|title=Historical Dictionary of Shinto|date=2010-12-28|publisher=Scarecrow Press|isbn=978-0-8108-7372-8|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Dougill|first=John|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-H_cEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT204|title=Off the Beaten Tracks in Japan: A Journey by Train from Hokkaido to Kyushu|date=2023-11-07|publisher=Stone Bridge Press, Inc.|isbn=978-1-61172-963-4|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Ponsonby-Fane|first=R. == Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture}}'s city of {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|en|Ichinomiya, Aichi|WD=Q270810|lt=Ichinomiya}}. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province}} (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|lt=Inazawa}}). Although the shrine is located in {{ill|Haguri District|en|Haguri District|WD=Q1032507|lt=Haguri District}} of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Sachihara|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}} annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}'s city of {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|en|Ichinomiya, Aichi|WD=Q270810|lt=Ichinomiya|1=Ichinomiya, Aichi}}. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province|1=Owari Province}} (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|lt=Inazawa|1=Inazawa}}). Although the shrine is located in {{ill|Haguri District|en|Haguri District|WD=Q1032507|lt=Haguri District|1=Haguri District}} of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Q128848565|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

More sources to add<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Authors|first=Various|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XEIiEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA534|title=RLE: Japan Mini-Set F: Philosophy and Religion (4 vols)|date=2021-03-18|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-90356-4|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nPaezHFlfNQC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT107|title=Where the Trees Grow Thick|isbn=978-0-595-28240-1|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Göttler|first1=Christine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uyk_DwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA437|title=The Nomadic Object: The Challenge of World for Early Modern Religious Art|last2=Mochizuki|first2=Mia|date=2017-11-06|publisher=BRILL|isbn=978-90-04-35450-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Picken|first=Stuart D. == Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu|1=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi|1=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus|1=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|1=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|1=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station|1=Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}'s city of {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|en|Ichinomiya, Aichi|WD=Q270810|lt=Ichinomiya|1=Ichinomiya, Aichi}}. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province|1=Owari Province}} (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|lt=Inazawa|1=Inazawa}}). Although the shrine is located in {{ill|Haguri District|en|Haguri District|WD=Q1032507|lt=Haguri District|1=Haguri District}} of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Q128848565|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu|1=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi|1=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus|1=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|1=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|1=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station|1=Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}'s city of {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|en|Ichinomiya, Aichi|WD=Q270810|lt=Ichinomiya|1=Ichinomiya, Aichi}}. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province|1=Owari Province}} (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|lt=Inazawa|1=Inazawa}}). Although the shrine is located in {{ill|Haguri District|en|Haguri District|WD=Q1032507|lt=Haguri District|1=Haguri District}} of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Q128848565|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu|1=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi|1=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus|1=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|1=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|1=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station|1=Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}'s city of {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|en|Ichinomiya, Aichi|WD=Q270810|lt=Ichinomiya|1=Ichinomiya, Aichi}}. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province|1=Owari Province}} (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|lt=Inazawa|1=Inazawa}}). Although the shrine is located in {{ill|Haguri District|en|Haguri District|WD=Q1032507|lt=Haguri District|1=Haguri District}} of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Q128848565|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu|1=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi|1=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus|1=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|1=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|1=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station|1=Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}'s city of {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|en|Ichinomiya, Aichi|WD=Q270810|lt=Ichinomiya|1=Ichinomiya, Aichi}}. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province|1=Owari Province}} (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|lt=Inazawa|1=Inazawa}}). Although the shrine is located in {{ill|Haguri District|en|Haguri District|WD=Q1032507|lt=Haguri District|1=Haguri District}} of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Q128848565|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu|1=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi|1=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus|1=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|1=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|1=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station|1=Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}'s city of {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|en|Ichinomiya, Aichi|WD=Q270810|lt=Ichinomiya|1=Ichinomiya, Aichi}}. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province|1=Owari Province}} (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|lt=Inazawa|1=Inazawa}}). Although the shrine is located in {{ill|Haguri District|en|Haguri District|WD=Q1032507|lt=Haguri District|1=Haguri District}} of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Q128848565|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu|1=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi|1=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus|1=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|1=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|1=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station|1=Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}'s city of {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|en|Ichinomiya, Aichi|WD=Q270810|lt=Ichinomiya|1=Ichinomiya, Aichi}}. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province|1=Owari Province}} (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|lt=Inazawa|1=Inazawa}}). Although the shrine is located in {{ill|Haguri District|en|Haguri District|WD=Q1032507|lt=Haguri District|1=Haguri District}} of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Q128848565|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

More sources to add<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Authors|first=Various|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XEIiEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA534|title=RLE: Japan Mini-Set F: Philosophy and Religion (4 vols)|date=2021-03-18|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-90356-4|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nPaezHFlfNQC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT107|title=Where the Trees Grow Thick|isbn=978-0-595-28240-1|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Göttler|first1=Christine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uyk_DwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA437|title=The Nomadic Object: The Challenge of World for Early Modern Religious Art|last2=Mochizuki|first2=Mia|date=2017-11-06|publisher=BRILL|isbn=978-90-04-35450-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Picken|first=Stuart D. == Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu|1=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi|1=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus|1=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|1=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|1=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station|1=Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}'s city of {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|en|Ichinomiya, Aichi|WD=Q270810|lt=Ichinomiya|1=Ichinomiya, Aichi}}. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province|1=Owari Province}} (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|lt=Inazawa|1=Inazawa}}). Although the shrine is located in {{ill|Haguri District|en|Haguri District|WD=Q1032507|lt=Haguri District|1=Haguri District}} of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Q128848565|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

More sources to add<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Authors|first=Various|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XEIiEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA534|title=RLE: Japan Mini-Set F: Philosophy and Religion (4 vols)|date=2021-03-18|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-90356-4|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nPaezHFlfNQC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT107|title=Where the Trees Grow Thick|isbn=978-0-595-28240-1|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Göttler|first1=Christine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uyk_DwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA437|title=The Nomadic Object: The Challenge of World for Early Modern Religious Art|last2=Mochizuki|first2=Mia|date=2017-11-06|publisher=BRILL|isbn=978-90-04-35450-0|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Picken|first=Stuart D. B.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BY23AwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA555|title=Studies In Shinto & Shrines|date=2014-06-03|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-89294-3|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Army|first=United States Department of the|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PvgsAAAAIAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=RA3-PA147|title=Pamphlet - Dept. of the Army|date=1945|publisher=Headquarters, Department of the Army.|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MVHoAAAAMAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA147|title=Department of the Army Pamphlet|date=1945|publisher=The Department|language=en}}</ref>

== Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu|1=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi|1=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus|1=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|1=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|1=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station|1=Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.

'''Sakate Shrine''' (坂手神社) is a Shinto shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|WD=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture|1=Aichi Prefecture}}'s city of {{ill|Ichinomiya, Aichi|en|Ichinomiya, Aichi|WD=Q270810|lt=Ichinomiya|1=Ichinomiya, Aichi}}. It was formerly designated as a prefectural shrine under the old shrine ranking system.

[[Sakate Shrine]] is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|1=Moto-Ise Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}}

The shrine appears in the {{ill|Engi-shiki|de|Engi-shiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi-shiki|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11064932}} as the Shikinaisha "Sakate Shrine" of Nakashima District, {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|WD=Q514506|lt=Owari Province|1=Owari Province}} (another theory identifies {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|de|Hiyoshi-Schrein|ja|日吉社|zh|日吉社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiyoshi Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日吉大社|1=Hiyoshi Taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q656451}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|WD=Q389562|lt=Inazawa|1=Inazawa}}). Although the shrine is located in {{ill|Haguri District|en|Haguri District|WD=Q1032507|lt=Haguri District|1=Haguri District}} of Owari Province, it is believed to have been part of Nakashima District before the medieval period. The place name {{ill|Sachihara|de|Sachihara|ja|佐千原|zh|佐千原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sachihara|1=Q128848565|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q128848565}} is said to have evolved from Sakate → Satehara → Sachihara.

Until the Meiji era, the shrine received sacred textiles from the {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} annually. One theory holds that it once served as an administrative office (御厨) of Ise Grand Shrine. It is also said to have been the "Moto Ise" Nakashima-no-miya of Owari Province (another tradition identifies {{ill|Sakami Shrine|de|Sakami-Schrein|ja|酒見神社|zh|酒見神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakami Shrine|1=Sakemi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11644372}}).

{{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} that used to host Amaterasu before she was moved to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. Edward|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201|title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology|date=2007-02-28|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stalker|first=Nancy K.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62|title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan|date=2007-10-31|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0|language=en}}</ref> The first one was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社|1=Ōmiwa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q705542}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine|1=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).<ref name="greenshinto">{{Cite web|last=D|first=John|date=2011-08-10|title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu|url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/|access-date=2023-10-18|website=Green Shinto|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara）|url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine|access-date=2023-10-03|website=Nationwide location database|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/|access-date=2023-10-03|website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN|language=en}}</ref> Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually moving to other Moto-Ise shrines and then finally to [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]].<ref name=":0" />

More sources to add<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kidder|first=J. == Overview ==

* The date of foundation is unknown. In the 14th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|WD=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|WD=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime-no-mikoto|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}—while searching for a site to enshrine the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu|1=Amaterasu}}—traveled from Ikurakawa-no-miya (present-day {{ill|Tenjin Shrine|de|Tenjin-Schrein|ja|天神神社|zh|天神神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenjin Shrine|1=Tenjin Jinja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11443287}}, Mizuho) to Nakashima District in Owari Province. It is said she first enshrined the Sakate deity here and placed Amaterasu’s spirit in a temporary shrine just north of the present site.
* During the Edo period it was known as {{ill|Hakken-sha|de|Hakken-sha|ja|八剣社|zh|八剣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakken-sha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八剣神社|1=Yatsurugi Shrine (disambiguation)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11390593}}, but in 1872 (Meiji 5) it was designated a village shrine and in 1941 (Shōwa 16) promoted to a prefectural shrine.

== Deity ==

* {{ill|Takamizukami|de|Takamizukami|ja|高水上神|zh|高水上神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takamizukami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
* Considered a son of {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|en|Ōyamatsumi|WD=Q386563|WD=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi|1=Ōyamatsumi}}.

== Access ==

* Take the {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|en|Meitetsu Bus|WD=Q6810397|lt=Meitetsu Bus|1=Meitetsu Bus}} to the "Sachihara" stop (15 min walk) or the "Higashi-Sachihara" stop (10 min walk).
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|en|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q2856589|lt=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|1=Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station}} (platform 3, bus terminal) on the {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|en|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|WD=Q1137838|lt=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|1=Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line}} & Bisai Line and {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|en|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|WD=Q871495|lt=JR Owari-Ichinomiya Station|1=Owari-Ichinomiya Station}}.
** Buses bound for "Miyata-hongo" stop at Sachihara; those bound for "Kawashima" stop at Higashi-Sachihara.
